record.paper_title: Frequently hypercyclic operators: recent advances and open problems
record.original_question: For a frequently hypercyclic operator T on a Banach space X, let FHC(T) denote the set of frequently hypercyclic vectors, meaning vectors x whose orbit visits every nonempty open set with positive lower density. Can there exist a Banach-space operator T such that every vector of X is the sum of two frequently hypercyclic vectors, i.e. X = FHC(T) + FHC(T)?

evidence.quote:
Problem 2. Is there an operator T on a Banach space X for which X = FHC (T ) +
FHC (T ) holds?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a separable infinite-dimensional Banach space and let $T:X\to X$ be a bounded linear operator. A vector $x\in X$ is called frequently hypercyclic for $T$ if for every nonempty open set $U\subseteq X$ the set $\{n\in\mathbb{N}: T^n x\in U\}$ has positive lower density, i.e.
$$\liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac{\#\{1\le n\le N: T^n x\in U\}}{N}>0.$$
The operator $T$ is said to be frequently hypercyclic if it admits at least one frequently hypercyclic vector. Denote by $\mathrm{FHC}(T)$ the set of all frequently hypercyclic vectors for $T$, and define
$$\mathrm{FHC}(T)+\mathrm{FHC}(T)=\{x+y: x,y\in \mathrm{FHC}(T)\}.$$
Question: Does there exist a separable Banach space $X$ and a bounded linear operator $T:X\to X$ such that
$$X=\mathrm{FHC}(T)+\mathrm{FHC}(T),$$
that is, every vector of $X$ can be written as the sum of two frequently hypercyclic vectors of $T$?
artifact.status_search_result: This is listed as an open problem in the literature on frequently hypercyclic operators. Web searches do not surface a resolution. Related results (e.g., decomposing operators as sums of frequently hypercyclic operators) are known, but the vector-level decomposition $X=\mathrm{FHC}(T)+\mathrm{FHC}(T)$ appears to remain unresolved. The set of frequently hypercyclic vectors is known to often be only of first Baire category, suggesting the question is nontrivial.

status_evidence.title: Common frequent hypercyclicity
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of the set FHC(T) of frequently hypercyclic vectors and its category/density properties.
status_evidence.claim: FHC(T) is often only of first Baire category, making sum-decomposition questions nontrivial.

status_evidence.title: Frequently hypercyclic operators (Bayart-Grivaux)
status_evidence.snippet: Foundational paper introducing frequently hypercyclic operators and FHC(T).
status_evidence.claim: Defines the framework and FHC(T) without resolving whether X=FHC(T)+FHC(T) can hold.
